ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diameter AB of the circle $\odot O$ forms an angle $\angle A=30^\circ$ with the chord AC, where $AC=CP$. $CP$ is a tangent to $\odot O$; if $PC=6$, what is the area of the shaded region in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Since $AC=PC$,

it follows that $\angle P=\angle A=30^\circ$,

thus $\angle COB=60^\circ$ and $OP=2OC$.

Given $PC=6$,

we have $OP^2-OC^2=6^2$,

which leads to $OC=2\sqrt{3}$.

Therefore, the area of the shaded region in the diagram $S_{\triangle POC}-S_{\text{sector} COB}$

$=\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 2\sqrt{3}-\frac{60^\circ \cdot \pi \times (2\sqrt{3})^2}{360^\circ}=6\sqrt{3}-2\pi$.

Hence, the area of the shaded region in the diagram is $\boxed{6\sqrt{3}-2\pi}$.
